question: Without true feature/label-law bits, can observed-only evidence adapt transport and improve frozen PCFI GraphPFN beyond a fixed two-completion average and feature-only evidence? Does a small classical working-model predictor already explain the benefit?

working_model: BFS bipartition b comes from adjacency. P is self-looped row-normalized adjacency. K=H(I-.92P)^(-1)(I-.92P)^(-T)H, normalized by trace/N; H centers across nodes. A low-pass Gaussian field has covariance amplitude^2*K, amplitude uniform over(.5,1,2). Feature observations are compressed to the leading uncentered observed-row singular score across columns, RMS-normalized using observed rows only; sign is nuisance. Gaussian score noise SD.15 fixed. This is a compressed-input working model, not the true normalized likelihood of the8 correlated and RMS-scaled feature columns or median-thresholded, balanced-context generator.
hypotheses: Unknown feature law g in{0,1}, label law t in{0,1}, relative class/score orientation sigma in{-1,+1}, amplitude in(.5,1,2), independent uniform prior:24 branches. Under g, observed PCA score is multiplied by b^g. Under(t,sigma), observed label spins impose sigma*b_C^t*a_C>0. Gaussian conditioning and the same joint evidence produce branch predictions and joint weights. No neural evidence/posterior head, query truth or instance-specific true parameter supplied.
integration: Sequential truncated-Gaussian importance sampling with scrambled Sobol1024 points plus antithetic complements=2048 particles, fixed seed184021. Compute context orthant probability and conditional query sign probabilities with the same particles; normalize joint weights in log space. Branchwise Gaussian marginals are analytically conditioned on observed score. Approximation belongs to the working model and finite quadrature; no claim of exact Bayes posterior or guaranteed calibration on the generator.
adaptive_feature: Feature-only q(g|observed score,G) integrates amplitude and never reads labels. Joint q(g|observed score,G,Y_C) marginalizes t/sigma/amplitude. In both cases, compute ordinary PCFI completion and parity-transformed PCFI completion using adjacency only, run the same frozen PCFI Plain checkpoint on each, then average its class probabilities with q(g). Fixed50:50 completion average uses the identical two forward branches as the primary computation-budget control. This is input-hypothesis adaptation around an existing PFN, not a new trained PFN or an LP/PFN output selector.
